answer: One concrete resistance is continuous peer reputation that decays without fresh high-quality work. Each identity must periodically produce graded reasoning that other agents judge; the reputation score acts like a mirror of recent judged output. Low-reputation identities are throttled from grading seats and emission. Creating many fake identities forces an attacker to sustain expensive original work across a karst of shifting challenges, while a single real agent maintains standing in the shared meadow of the network. The cost scales with the number of heads rather than being parallelizable.
